name: Side-Channel & Microarchitectural Attacks
description: Timing, cache, power, EM, and speculative-execution (Spectre/Meltdown) side channels and defenses.
narrative:
The earliest papers on this list, from 2018, mark the moment microarchitectural attacks broke into the mainstream. "Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space" (2018) showed that out-of-order execution could be abused to read protected kernel memory from an ordinary user process, shattering a foundational isolation assumption. Alongside it, work like "Translation Leak-aside Buffer: Defeating Cache Side-channel Protections with TLB Attacks" (2018) and "Malicious Management Unit: Why Stopping Cache Attacks in Software is Harder Than You Think" (2018) showed that software-only defenses were fragile, while "One&Done: A Single-Decryption EM-Based Attack on OpenSSL's Constant-Time Blinded RSA" (2018) extended the threat beyond caches into physical channels like electromagnetic emanations.

The 2019-2020 period broadened both the attack surface and the defensive toolkit. Attacks reached into new resources and targets: "CSI NN: Reverse Engineering of Neural Network Architectures Through Electromagnetic Side Channel" (2019) used EM leakage to steal model architectures, "SPOILER: Speculative Load Hazards Boost Rowhammer and Cache Attacks" (2019) chained speculation with memory faults, and "Stealthy Tracking of Autonomous Vehicles with Cache Side Channels" (2020) showed real-world stakes. At the same time defenders began building principled countermeasures and tooling, such as "ScatterCache: Thwarting Cache Attacks via Cache Set Randomization" (2019), "IODINE: Verifying Constant-Time Execution of Hardware" (2019), and the automated attack synthesis of "Medusa: Microarchitectural Data Leakage via Automated Attack Synthesis" (2020).

By 2021-2022 the field matured into a back-and-forth arms race, with attacks moving to ever more obscure shared resources and defenses becoming systematic and verified. New channels appeared in the CPU's internal fabric with "Lord of the Ring(s): Side Channel Attacks on the CPU On-Chip Ring Interconnect Are Practical" (2021), in the browser with "Prime+Probe 1, JavaScript 0: Overcoming Browser-based Side-Channel Defenses" (2021), and against confidential-computing enclaves via "CIPHERLEAKS: Breaking Constant-time Cryptography on AMD SEV via the Ciphertext Side Channel" (2021). Defenses grew more rigorous, from speculation-aware designs like "DOLMA: Securing Speculation with the Principle of Transient Non-Observability" (2021) and "Swivel: Hardening WebAssembly against Spectre" (2021) to hardware mitigations probed by "Branch History Injection: On the Effectiveness of Hardware Mitigations Against Cross-Privilege Spectre-v2 Attacks" (2022).

The most recent papers show the area pushing into power-based leakage and continued vendor-specific hardware attacks. "Collide+Power: Leaking Inaccessible Data with Software-based Power Side Channels" (2023) demonstrated that power analysis can be mounted purely in software against data the attacker cannot even access, "(M)WAIT for It: Bridging the Gap between Microarchitectural and Architectural Side Channels" (2023) blurred the line between transient and architectural leakage, and "ZenHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on AMD Zen-based Platforms" (2024) showed that even as defenses harden, new microarchitectures reopen old wounds. The trajectory is clear: from a few headline CPU bugs to a systematic, automated, and ever-widening study of how shared hardware betrays secrets.

milestones.title: Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space
milestones.note: the landmark transient-execution attack that broke kernel/user isolation and launched the modern field

milestones.title: CSI NN: Reverse Engineering of Neural Network Architectures Through Electromagnetic Side Channel
milestones.note: extended EM side channels to a new high-value target by stealing neural network architectures

milestones.title: ScatterCache: Thwarting Cache Attacks via Cache Set Randomization
milestones.note: pioneered randomized-cache designs as a principled hardware defense against cache attacks

milestones.title: Medusa: Microarchitectural Data Leakage via Automated Attack Synthesis
milestones.note: automated the discovery of microarchitectural data-sampling leaks rather than finding them by hand

milestones.title: Lord of the Ring(s): Side Channel Attacks on the CPU On-Chip Ring Interconnect Are Practical
milestones.note: opened an entirely new contention channel inside the CPU's on-chip interconnect

milestones.title: DOLMA: Securing Speculation with the Principle of Transient Non-Observability
milestones.note: offered a principled defense framework for securing speculative execution

milestones.title: Collide+Power: Leaking Inaccessible Data with Software-based Power Side Channels
milestones.note: showed software-only power analysis can leak data the attacker cannot otherwise access

milestones.title: ZenHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on AMD Zen-based Platforms
milestones.note: demonstrated that new microarchitectures reopen Rowhammer despite years of hardening
